title: gpu-surge-control-policy-and-prefetch-degradation-mitigation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity event on 2026-02-27 we observed multi-region GPU pools reach sustained saturation causing request queue buildup, token-level throttling, and elevated tail latencies. Root cause analysis indicates a confluence of factors: (1) an unexpected traffic pattern spike with many long-context generation requests (heavy KV cache pressure); (2) autoscaler smoothing windows that delayed scale-up by ~90-120s; (3) the admission controller allowed a mix of low-priority, large-batch jobs that monopolized GPU slots; (4) KV cache miss amplification due to a new model rollout with different tokenization cadence. The incident produced broad customer impact for mid-tier hosted API customers and increased error budget burn. This ticket tracks follow-ups: short-term operational mitigations, scheduler and admission control fixes, autoscaler tuning, and follow-through testing and runbook updates.
action_items: Hotfix: deploy emergency admission policy (reject-or-queue-low-priority) to reduce new inflight long-context jobs in saturated pools — rolled to production 2026-03-02 (PR #1258)
Autoscaler: reduce scale-up smoothing window from 120s -> 30s for burstable pools and add fast-path on CPU+queue-size metric (owner: Marcus) — proposal PR #1283
Scheduler: implement prioritized eviction for non-SLO traffic (preemptible jobs) and ensure KV cache warm-up reservation for canary traffic (owner: Priya Rao)
Telemetry: add per-pool queue-length and per-customer inflight-requests metrics with 10s granularity; surface in Console alerts and run automated paged alerts when queue > 50 for > 60s
Admission controller: introduce token-based per-customer concurrency caps and reject with explicit 429 + retry-after header (owner: backend infra)
Model onboarding: require tokenization/sequence-length distribution benchmarks in model catalog before full rollout; add canary ratio cap to new-model deploys
Backpressure UX: update client SDKs to expose early-fail semantics and client-side retry/backoff guidance in docs
Runbook: update hosted-gpu-exhaustion runbook with new mitigation play (emergency admission toggle, autoscaler fast-path, prioritized eviction steps); schedule on-call drill
Chaos testing: add a synthetic workload in staging that simulates high long-context variance and low-KV-hit-rate to validate autoscaler/scheduler behavior pre-release
Post-incident review: complete customer impact timeline, notify affected customers, and attach regression detection checks to CI for scheduling/ads changes
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Chen: Emergency admission policy deployed to affected GPU pools at 03:14 UTC; immediate queue drain observed and 95th pct latency improved by ~420ms. Notified SRE and product teams.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Patel: Draft autoscaler tuning changes pushed in PR #1283; running canary in eu-west-1 with synthetic traffic. Early results: scale-up latency reduced to ~22s for the canary workload.
2026-03-04 - Sofia Ramirez (PM): Notified top 5 impacted customers with interim mitigation summary and ETA for permanent fixes. Requested follow-up call with two enterprise customers.
2026-03-06 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Added queue-length dashboards to Console (private link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/gpu-queue); alerts configured and validated.
2026-03-09 - Marcus Patel: Scheduler preemption prototype merged to staging (PR #1310). Behavior: preempt lowest-priority batches within 5s; requires upgrade to runtime-1.20 on serving nodes.
2026-03-12 - Ava Chen: This ticket is tracking remaining work for autoscaler rollout and model onboarding guardrails. Blocking: final QA on eviction safety and client SDK docs.
2026-03-12 - Marcus Patel: Dependency ENG-30912 referenced for priority-aware credit admission; coordinating handoff for integration tests.
